definition: Different raw names, identical after case folding.
Case-folded names differ but alphanumeric token sequences agree.
Token sequences differ but agree after Unicode accent removal.
Unicode letter scripts differ; may be transliteration or translation, not verified.
Matched name contains letters from multiple scripts.
Legal-form token counts differ; may overlap other name changes.
Name tokens become equal under the small documented abbreviation map.
Same token multiset but different sequence.
A matched-name token of at least two characters repeats more often than in S1; single-letter initial fragments are excluded.
One name's token multiset is a strict subset of the other.
Same-script nonidentical normalized names have character similarity >= 0.72; excludes pure reorder/subset cases.
A differing token agrees after 0->o, 1->i, 3->e, 4->a, 5->s, 7->t substitution.
Changed name includes a URL, .com/.in domain, or hashtag marker.
Matched name has a standalone digit sequence absent from S1; possible appended identifier.
Name token sequences differ but concatenating their normalized tokens yields identical text.
Matched name reduces to one 2-8 character token equal to the initials of S1 tokens after removing legal-form tokens.
Matched name adds Mr/Mrs/Ms/Dr/Shri/Sri tokens absent from S1.
Changed name includes DBA, formerly, or trading-as text.
Nonempty normalized names share at most 25% of their token union.
One name is empty or a whole-field null marker.
One address is empty or a whole-field null marker.
Different raw addresses have the same alphanumeric token sequence.
Address Unicode letter scripts differ; not a verified transliteration.
Raw address token multiset differs but agrees after abbreviation/US-state normalization.
Normalized address tokens have the same multiset but a different sequence.
One normalized address token multiset is a strict subset of the other.
Nonempty addresses have different digit-token multisets; may be formatting, unit, postcode, or house-number changes.
Apartment/unit/suite/floor/PO-box/PMB marker counts differ.
Address contains null/none/nan as a token within other text.
Near/opposite/opp/behind/beside landmark-marker counts differ.
Digit-token sequences differ but agree after stripping leading zeros.
Same-script normalized addresses differ with character similarity >= 0.80, excluding identical token multisets.
Nonempty addresses share at most 25% of their normalized token union; not proof of relocation.
Each US address has one unambiguous comma-delimited state token and they disagree; review manually.
States agree, conservative city extraction succeeds, and city similarity is < 0.75; review manually.
Ground-truth-linked records have different case-folded country labels.
At least one country is empty or a whole-field null marker.
Name, address, and country are exactly identical.
Text differs but no other detector fired.
S1 has an empty ground-truth match list; retained as a control.
